text:
A8 done, commit 936e878. `./gradlew assembleDebug lint test` green: 0 lint
errors, same 23 pre-existing warnings as A5-A7. 81 unit tests / 17 suites,
all passing.

Two genuine Robolectric-Compose-testing gotchas hit and fixed here, worth
knowing for A9/A10/A11 (which all add more dialogs/forms):

1. Never stack two `AlertDialog`s simultaneously (e.g. a confirm dialog
   rendered as a second `if (...) { AlertDialog(...) }` appended after the
   main one). Each AlertDialog is its own Window/root; with two active,
   `composeTestRule.onRoot()` throws ("expected exactly 1 node but found
   2 that satisfy isRoot"), and — the more insidious part — clicks
   silently no-op instead of throwing, so a naive test just times out or
   fails a downstream assertion with no clue why. Fix: make dialogs
   mutually exclusive (`if (x) A else B`), never simultaneous.

2. Robolectric's simulated dialog viewport is tiny (observed 320x470px
   for this project's AlertDialogs). Any dialog with more than ~4-5
   fields in a `Modifier.verticalScroll(rememberScrollState())` Column
   will have its lower content start out scrolled off-screen.
   `composeTestRule.onNodeWithText(...).performClick()` computes a click
   at the node's *layout* bounds regardless of scroll position — clicking
   a node that exists-but-is-scrolled-out-of-view silently hits nothing
   (no exception, just no effect). Always chain
   `.performScrollTo().performClick()` for anything inside a scrollable
   dialog body, not just `.performClick()` alone. This will matter again
   for A9's list-properties screen and A10's settings dialog, both of
   which sound field-heavy per Notes.

Design note for A9 (share/list props) and A11 (registry): ItemFormViewModel
+ EditItemDialog are meant to be reused as-is from the list's registry
view (A11) and anywhere else an existing item needs editing — no new
per-screen edit-form code should be needed, just `EditItemDialog(itemId =
..., onDismiss = ...)`. AddItemDialog similarly only needs a `listId`.

ItemDao gained `findByExactName(listId, name, excludingId)` (excludingId
takes an empty-string sentinel, not null, since real ids are UUIDs) for
the case-insensitive per-list name-uniqueness pre-check. Any future
ticket needing "does this name already exist" logic (e.g. list rename in
A9, though that's list-level not item-level and has no such constraint
per the spec) should reuse this rather than re-deriving it from
searchRegistry's substring search.
